title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview as a free open-weights model with a commercial license

sources.name: Baidu ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Preview Hugging Face model card

kept.claim: Baidu released the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview model weights under the Apache License 2.0.
kept.evidence: [0] 'ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview is released under the Apache License 2.0'. [1] Baidu 'released ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview under the Apache 2.0 license'. [2] weights are published under Apache 2.0.

kept.claim: The Apache 2.0 licence allows commercial use, modification and redistribution, and developers do not pay Baidu per interaction. (Source 0 names the licence but does not spell out these terms. Source 2 is derived from Decrypt.)
kept.evidence: [1] 'allowing commercial use, modification and redistribution'; developers can use it 'without paying Baidu for every interaction'. [2] letting developers download, modify and build commercial products on it without paying Baidu per interaction, citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The model is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 280B total parameters and 14B active per token.
kept.evidence: [0] '280B total parameters, 14B of them active per token'. [1] 280 billion parameters, 14 billion used per token. [2] 280-billion-parameter MoE with 14 billion active per token.

kept.claim: The context window is 1M tokens (1,048,576 in the spec table).
kept.evidence: [0] '1M-token context window'; table shows 'Context Length 1,048,576'. [1] 'context window exceeds one million tokens'. [2] 'context window exceeds one million tokens'.

kept.claim: Most of the weights are compressed to 4-bit precision (FP4 / MXFP4 routed experts), and the model uses speculative decoding with a DSpark draft head.
kept.evidence: [0] routed experts in MXFP4 (W4A8); 'adds a DSpark draft head for speculative decoding'. [1] compressed most weights to four-bit precision and used speculative decoding. [2] repeats this, citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The model card describes the Preview as an intermediate checkpoint from post-training. Some capabilities may fall short because training is not finished, and an official release will follow.
kept.evidence: [0] 'an intermediate checkpoint from post-training'. [2] quotes the same Baidu model-card wording.

kept.claim: The model is text in, text out. It cannot process images natively.
kept.evidence: [0] spec table says 'Modality: Text in, text out' (implies this but does not say images are unsupported). [1] the model worked 'despite being unable to process images natively'. [2] repeats this.

kept.claim: Baidu's demo: in a single 11-hour coding task the model wrote a third-person wuxia/martial-arts game on Unreal Engine 5.8.
kept.evidence: [0] 'In a single 11-hour coding task it wrote a complete third-person wuxia game in C++ on Unreal Engine 5.8'. [1] and [2] describe an 11-hour Unreal Engine 5.8 martial-arts game build.

kept.claim: Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview 46.5, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 42.3, GLM-5.3-Flash 35.8, GPT-6.1 Sol 56.1.
kept.evidence: [0] benchmark table row 46.5 / 42.3 / 35.8 / 56.1. [1] 46.5%, 42.3%, 35.8%, 56.1%. [2] same figures, citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: AutomationBench scores: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview 61.9, GPT-6.1 Sol 49.3, Claude Opus 5.5 58.0.
kept.evidence: [0] table row 61.9 / 49.3* / 58.0*. [1] 61.9% vs 49.3% for GPT and 58% for Claude. [2] same figures, citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The benchmark results are Baidu's own, manufacturer-reported evaluations.
kept.evidence: [0] 'All ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview scores are from our own evaluations.' [1] 'manufacturer-reported results'. [2] benchmarks 'still self-reported'.

kept.claim: Baidu's international API pricing is $0.28 per million input tokens and $1.13 per million output tokens. Decrypt links this to a third-party blog, and the Hugging Face card gives no pricing.
kept.evidence: [1] 'pricing is $0.28 per million input tokens and $1.13 per million output tokens'. [2] same figures, citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The model is also available through a free tier on OpenRouter.
kept.evidence: [1] 'available through a free tier on OpenRouter'. [2] 'a free tier available through OpenRouter', citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The announcement is older than the weights release. Baidu introduced the Preview through its cloud platform roughly two weeks before the open weights were published.
kept.evidence: [1] 'The release comes nearly two weeks after Baidu introduced the model through its cloud computing platform.' [2] 'roughly two weeks before publishing its open weights', citing Decrypt.

kept.claim: The open-weights release date: Decrypt (published Nov 25, 2026) says 'this week'. The Machine Herald (Nov 26, 2026) says the Hugging Face repository was created on November 23, 2026.
kept.evidence: [1] 'released its ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview AI model this week', dated Nov 25, 2026. [2] repository for the BF16 weights 'was created on November 23, 2026'. Only [2] gives the Nov 23 date.

dropped.claim: The Apache 2.0 licence covers the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights only. ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base stays under its own licence, the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base Model License Agreement v1.0.
dropped.evidence: [0] License section: 'This license covers the ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview weights only.' Single source.

dropped.claim: The Hugging Face page's auto-generated metadata and sidebar list the model size as '300B params'. This differs from the 280B stated in the card text and by the press.
dropped.evidence: [0] The page description says 'Text Generation model with 300B parameters', and the sidebar shows 'Model size 300B params'. The card text says 280B.

dropped.claim: ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base was released earlier, on November 5, as a raw pre-trained model with 33.5 trillion training tokens. Source 0 says only that the Base was 'released earlier'.
dropped.evidence: [2] cites The Decoder for the Nov 5 Base release and 33.5T tokens. [0] says the Base was released earlier but gives no date. Not confirmed by two sources.

dropped.claim: Baidu says the model generates more than 200 tokens per second.
dropped.evidence: [1] 'generating more than 200 tokens per second, according to Baidu'. Single source.

dropped.claim: No independent third-party reproduction of Baidu's benchmark numbers exists yet. Artificial Analysis had no entry for the model as of Nov 26, 2026.
dropped.evidence: [2] 'None of the cited sources show an independent, third-party reproduction'. Single source.

dropped.claim: The release is open-weight rather than fully open-source, because it does not provide everything needed to reproduce the model's training.
dropped.evidence: [2] states this, attributing it to Decrypt. I did not locate this wording in Decrypt, so single source.
